part.p: Agencies procuring high assurance products and HACE MUST contact the GCSB and comply with any product specific delivery procedures.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD ensure that products are delivered in a manner consistent with any delivery procedures defined in associated documentation.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD ensure that products purchased without the delivery assurances provided through the use of formally evaluated procedures are delivered in a manner that provides confidence that they receive the product that they expect to receive in an unaltered state, including checking:

ul.li: any labelling changes;
any damage; and
any signs of tampering.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD ensure that leasing agreements for IT equipment takes into account the:

ul.li: difficulties that could be encountered when the equipment needs maintenance;
control of remote maintenance, software updates and fault diagnosis;
if the equipment can be easily sanitised prior to its return; and
the possible requirement for destruction if sanitisation cannot be performed.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD choose products from developers that have made a commitment to the ongoing maintenance of the assurance of their product.

group.title: Installation and configuration of evaluated products

control.title: 12.2.5.C.01. — Installation and configuration of evaluated products

prop.name: topic
prop.value: Installation and configuration of evaluated products

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST ensure that high assurance products and HACE are installed, configured, operated and administered in accordance with all product specific policy.

control.title: 12.2.5.C.02. — Installation and configuration of evaluated products

prop.name: topic
prop.value: Installation and configuration of evaluated products

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD install, configure, operate and administer evaluated products in accordance with available documentation resulting from the product’s evaluation.

group.title: Use of evaluated products in unevaluated configurations

control.title: 12.2.6.C.01. — Use of evaluated products in unevaluated configurations

prop.name: topic
prop.value: Use of evaluated products in unevaluated configurations

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies wishing to use a product in an unevaluated configuration MUST undertake a security risk assessment including:

ul.li: the necessity of the unevaluated configuration;
testing of the unevaluated configuration; and
the environment in which the unevaluated product is to be used.

control.title: 12.2.6.C.02. — Use of evaluated products in unevaluated configurations

prop.name: topic
prop.value: Use of evaluated products in unevaluated configurations

part.name: statement
part.p: High assurance products and HACE MUST NOT be used in unevaluated configurations.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST classify IT equipment based on the highest classification of information the equipment and any associated media within the equipment, are approved for processing, storing or communicating.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST clearly label all IT equipment in data centres or computer rooms with an asset identification and the level of classification to which that equipment has been accredited.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST NOT have any non-essential labels applied to external surfaces of high assurance products.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD seek GCSB authorisation before applying labels to external surfaces of HACE.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD monitor relevant sources for information about new vulnerabilities and security patches for software and IT equipment used by the agency.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST implement a patch management strategy, including an evaluation or testing process.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST NOT patch high assurance products or HACE without the patch being approved by the GCSB.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD apply all critical security patches as soon as possible and preferably within two (2) days of the release of the patch or update.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD apply all non-critical security patches as soon as possible.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD ensure that security patches are applied through a vendor recommended patch or upgrade process.

group.title: When security patches are not available

control.title: 12.4.5.C.01. — When security patches are not available

prop.name: topic
prop.value: When security patches are not available

part.name: statement
part.p: Where known vulnerabilities cannot be patched, or security patches are not available, agencies SHOULD implement:

ul.li: controls to resolve the vulnerability such as:
disable the functionality associated with the vulnerability though product configuration;
ask the vendor for an alternative method of managing the vulnerability;
install a version of the product that does not have the identified vulnerability;
install a different product with a more responsive vendor; or
engage a software developer to correct the software.
controls to prevent exploitation of the vulnerability including:
apply external input sanitisation (if an input triggers the exploit);
apply filtering or verification on the software output (if the exploit relates to an information disclosure);
apply additional access controls that prevent access to the vulnerability; or
configure firewall rules to limit access to the vulnerable software.
controls to contain the exploit including:
apply firewall rules limiting outward traffic that is likely in the event of an exploitation;
apply mandatory access control preventing the execution of exploitation code; or
set file system permissions preventing exploitation code from being written to disk;
allow and deny listing to prevent code execution; and
controls to detect attacks including:
deploy an IDS;
monitor logging alerts; or
use other mechanisms as appropriate for the detection of exploits using the known vulnerability.
controls to prevent attacks including:
deploy an IPS or HIPS; or
use other mechanisms as appropriate for the diversion of exploits using the known vulnerability, such as honey pots and Null routers.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST ensure that any firmware updates are performed in a manner that verifies the integrity and authenticity of the source and of the updating process or updating utility.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD assess the security risk of continued use of software or IT equipment when a cessation date for support is announced or when the product is no longer supported by the developer.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST seek GCSB approval before undertaking any repairs to high assurance products or HACE.

part.name: statement
part.p: Maintenance and repairs of IT equipment containing media SHOULD be carried out on-site by an appropriately cleared technician.

group.title: Maintenance and repairs by an uncleared technician

control.title: 12.5.4.C.01. — Maintenance and repairs by an uncleared technician

prop.name: topic
prop.value: Maintenance and repairs by an uncleared technician

part.name: statement
part.p: If an uncleared technician is used to undertake maintenance or repairs of IT equipment, the technician MUST be escorted by someone who:

ul.li: is appropriately cleared and briefed;
takes due care to ensure that classified information is not disclosed;
takes all responsible measures to ensure the integrity of the equipment; and
has the authority to direct the technician.

control.title: 12.5.4.C.02. — Maintenance and repairs by an uncleared technician

prop.name: topic
prop.value: Maintenance and repairs by an uncleared technician

part.name: statement
part.p: If an uncleared technician is used to undertake maintenance or repairs of IT equipment, agencies SHOULD sanitise and reclassify or declassify the equipment and associated media before maintenance or repair work is undertaken.

control.title: 12.5.4.C.03. — Maintenance and repairs by an uncleared technician

prop.name: topic
prop.value: Maintenance and repairs by an uncleared technician

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD ensure that the ratio of escorts to uncleared technicians allows for appropriate oversight of all activities.

control.title: 12.5.4.C.04. — Maintenance and repairs by an uncleared technician

prop.name: topic
prop.value: Maintenance and repairs by an uncleared technician

part.name: statement
part.p: If an uncleared technician is used to undertake maintenance or repairs of IT equipment, the technician SHOULD be escorted by someone who is sufficiently familiar with the product to understand the work being performed.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies having IT equipment maintained or repaired off-site MUST ensure that the physical transfer, processing and storage requirements are appropriate for the classification of the product and are maintained at all times.

group.title: Maintenance and repair of IT equipment from secure areas

control.title: 12.5.6.C.01. — Maintenance and repair of IT equipment from secure areas

prop.name: topic
prop.value: Maintenance and repair of IT equipment from secure areas

part.name: statement
part.p: Offsite repairs and maintenance SHOULD treat all equipment in accordance with the requirements for the highest classification of information processed, stored or communicated in the area that the equipment will be returned to.

control.title: 12.5.6.C.02. — Maintenance and repair of IT equipment from secure areas

prop.name: topic
prop.value: Maintenance and repair of IT equipment from secure areas

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD conduct or arrange to have technical inspections conducted on all equipment returned to the secure area after maintenance or repair.

group.title: Sanitisation or destruction of IT equipment

control.title: 12.6.4.C.01. — Sanitisation or destruction of IT equipment

prop.name: topic
prop.value: Sanitisation or destruction of IT equipment

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST sanitise or destroy, then declassify, IT equipment containing any media before disposal.

control.title: 12.6.4.C.02. — Sanitisation or destruction of IT equipment

prop.name: topic
prop.value: Sanitisation or destruction of IT equipment

part.name: statement
part.p: IT equipment and associated media that have processed or stored NZEO information, and cannot be sanitised, MUST be returned to New Zealand for sanitisation or destruction, declassification and disposal.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST have a documented process for the disposal of IT equipment.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST contact the GCSB and comply with any requirements for the disposal of high assurance products.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST contact the GCSB and comply with any requirements for the disposal of HACE.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST contact GCSB and comply with any requirements for the disposal of TEMPEST rated IT equipment or if the equipment is non-functional.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST formally sanitise and then authorise the disposal of IT equipment, or waste, into the public domain.

group.title: Sanitising printer cartridges and copier drums

control.title: 12.6.6.C.02. — Sanitising printer cartridges and copier drums

prop.name: topic
prop.value: Sanitising printer cartridges and copier drums

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD print at least three pages of random text with no blank areas on each colour printer cartridge with an integrated drum or separate copier drum.

control.title: 12.6.7.C.02. — Destroying printer cartridges and copier drums

prop.name: topic
prop.value: Destroying printer cartridges and copier drums

part.p: Agencies unable to sanitise printer cartridges with integrated copier drums or discrete copier drums, SHOULD destroy the cartridge or drum.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST visually inspect video screens by turning up the brightness to the maximum level to determine if any classified information has been burnt into or persists on the screen, before redeployment or disposal.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST attempt to sanitise video screens with minor burn-in or image persistence by displaying a solid white image on the screen for an extended period of time. If burn-in cannot be corrected the screen MUST be processed through an approved destruction facility.

control.title: 12.6.10.C.01. — LCD/LED, plasma and non-CRT monitor types

prop.name: topic
prop.value: LCD/LED, plasma and non-CRT monitor types

part.name: statement
part.p: Because of the risks that data can be recovered from monitors, it is essential that any redeployment or disposal of monitors MUST follow the guidance in the NZISM.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD incorporate the consideration of supply chain risks into an organisation-wide risk assessment and management process.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD monitor supply chain risks on an ongoing basis and adjust mitigations and controls appropriately.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD follow the Government Rules of Procurement.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD require tenderers and contractors to provide information:

ul.li: identifying any restrictions on the disclosure, transfer or use of technology arising out of export controls or security arrangements; and
demonstrating that their supply chains comply with the security of supply requirements set out in the contract documents.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD request information from contractors and subcontractors to assess their ability to protect information.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD include contractual obligations to safeguard information throughout the tendering and contracting procedure.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD reject contractors and subcontractors where they do not possess the necessary reliability to exclude risks to national security; or have breached obligations relating to security of information during a previous contract in circumstances amounting to grave misconduct.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD ensure that changes in their supply chain during the performance of the contract will not adversely affect the continuity of supply requirements.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD require suppliers and contractors to provide the provenance of any products or equipment.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD validate the security of the equipment against security performance, capability and functionality requirements.

part.name: statement
part.p: Where deficiencies in security performance, capability and functionality are identified, agencies SHOULD implement additional risk mitigation measures.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD inspect equipment on receipt for any obvious signs of tampering, relabelling or damage.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD inspect equipment on receipt and test the operation before installation.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD conduct installation verification and related tests before the equipment is used in an operational system.

part.name: statement
part.p: Where any software, firmware or other forms of programme code are required for the initialisation, operation, servicing or maintenance of the equipment, malware checks SHOULD be conducted before the equipment is installed in an operational system.

part.name: statement
part.p: For equipment that is expected to have an extended operational life in a critical system, and in the event that the supplier is no longer able to supply these, agencies SHOULD provide for the acquisition of:

ul.li: necessary licences;
information to produce spare parts, components, assemblies;
testing equipment; and
technical assistance agreements.

group.title: 13. Media and IT Equipment Management, Decommissioning and Disposal

part.name: statement
part.p: When the Information System reaches the end of its service life in an organisation, policy and procedures SHOULD be in place to ensure secure decommissioning and transfer or disposal, in order to satisfy corporate, legal and statutory requirements.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD undertake a risk assessment with consideration given to proportionality in respect of:

ul.li: scale and impact of the processes;
data;
users;
licences;
usage agreements; and
service to be migrated or decommissioned.

part.name: statement
part.p: The risk assessment SHOULD include the following elements:

ul.li: Evaluation of the applications inventory and identification of any redundancies;
Identification of data owners and key stakeholders;
Identification of types of information (Active or Inactive) processed and stored;
Identification of software and other (including non-transferable) licences;
Identification of access rights to be transferred or cancelled;
Identification of any emanation control equipment or security enhancements;
Consideration of short and long term reporting requirements;
Assessment of equipment and hardware for redeployment or disposal;
Identification of any cloud-based data and services; and
User re-training.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD consider the need for a Privacy Impact Assessment.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD identify relevant service and legal agreements and arrange for their termination.

part.name: statement
part.p: The decommissioning plan will be based on the migration plan and SHOULD incorporate the following elements:

ul.li: An impact analysis;
Issue of notification to service providers, users and customers;
Issue of notification of decommissioning to all relevant interfaces and interconnections;
Timeframe, plan and schedule;
Data integrity and validation checks before archiving;
Transfer or redeployment of equipment and other assets;
Transfer or cancellation of licences;
Removal of redundant equipment and software;
Removal of redundant cables and termination equipment;
Removal of any emanation control equipment or security enhancements;
Return or safe disposal of any emanation control equipment or security enhancements;
Updates to systems configurations (switches, firewalls etc.);
Equipment and media sanitisation including any cloud-based data & services(discussed later in this chapter);
Equipment and media disposal (discussed later in this chapter);
Any legal considerations for supply or service contract terminations;
Asset register updates; and
Retraining for, or redeployment of, support staff.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD identify data retention policies, regulation and legislation.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD ensure adequate system documentation is archived.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD archive essential software, system logic, system documentation and other system data to allow information to be recovered from archive.

part.name: statement
part.p: The Agency’s Accreditation Authority SHOULD confirm IA compliance on decommissioning and disposal.

part.name: statement
part.p: The Agency’s Accreditation Authority SHOULD confirm secure equipment and media disposal.

part.name: statement
part.p: The Agency’s Accreditation Authority SHOULD confirm asset register updates.

part.name: statement
part.p: Once all security relevant activities associated with decommissioning and disposal have been completed and verified, a Security Decommissioning Compliance Certificate SHOULD be issued by the Agency’s Accreditation Authority.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD undertake a post-decommissioning review.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST document procedures for the reclassification and declassification of media.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST classify media to the highest classification of data stored on the media.

group.title: Classifying media connected to systems of higher classifications

control.title: 13.2.8.C.01. — Classifying media connected to systems of higher classifications

prop.name: topic
prop.value: Classifying media connected to systems of higher classifications

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST classify any media connected to a system of a higher classification at the higher system classification until confirmed not to be the case.

group.title: Classifying media below that of the system

control.title: 13.2.9.C.01. — Classifying media below that of the system

prop.name: topic
prop.value: Classifying media below that of the system

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies intending to classify media below the classification of the system to which it is connected to MUST ensure that:

ul.li: the media is read-only;
the media is inserted into a read-only device; or
the system has a mechanism through which read-only access can be assured such as approved data diodes, write-blockers or similar infrastructure.

group.title: Reclassifying media to a lower classification

control.title: 13.2.10.C.01. — Reclassifying media to a lower classification

prop.name: topic
prop.value: Reclassifying media to a lower classification

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies wishing to reclassify media to a lower classification MUST ensure that:

ul.li: a formal decision is made to reclassify, or redeploy the media; and
the reclassification of all information on the media has been approved by the originator, or the media has been appropriately sanitised or destroyed.

group.title: Reclassifying media to a higher classification

control.title: 13.2.11.C.01. — Reclassifying media to a higher classification

prop.name: topic
prop.value: Reclassifying media to a higher classification

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST reclassify media if:

ul.li: information copied onto the media is of a higher classification; or
information contained on the media is subjected to a classification upgrade.

part.name: statement
part.p: When using non-textual (colour, symbol) protective markings for operational security reasons, agencies MUST document the labelling scheme and train personnel appropriately.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD label media with a marking that indicates the maximum classification and any endorsements applicable to the information stored.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD register all media with a unique identifier in an appropriate register.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST ensure that storage facilities for media containing classified information meets the minimum physical security storage requirements as specified in the PSR Policy Framework - Physical Security.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST disable any automatic execution features within operating systems for connectable devices and media.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST prevent unauthorised media from connecting to a system via the use of:

ul.li: device access control software;
seals;
physical means; or
other methods approved by the Accreditation Authority.

part.name: statement
part.p: When writable media is connected to a writable communications port or device, agencies SHOULD implement controls to prevent the unintended writing of data to the media.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD disable IEEE 1394 interfaces.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST ensure that processes for transferring media containing classified information meets the minimum physical transfer requirements as specified in the PSR.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD encrypt data stored on media with at least an Approved Cryptographic Algorithm (See Section 17.2 – Approved Cryptographic Algorithms) if it is to be transferred to another area or location.

part.name: statement
part.p: Data transfers between systems of different classification SHOULD be logged in an auditable log or register.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies transferring data manually between two systems of different security domains or classifications SHOULD NOT use rewriteable media.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST document conditions and procedures for the sanitisation of media and IT Equipment.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST destroy the following media types prior to disposal, as they cannot be effectively sanitised:

ul.li: microfiche;
microfilm;
optical discs;
printer ribbons and the impact surface facing the platen;
programmable read-only memory (PROM, EPROM, EEPROM);
flash memory and solid state or hybrid data storage devices;
read-only memory; and
faulty magnetic media that cannot be successfully sanitised.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST sanitise volatile media by:

ul.li: overwriting all locations of the media with an arbitrary pattern;
followed by a read back for verification; and

part.name: statement
