group.title: Inverse split tunnel in remote access VPN systems

control.title: 18.7.14.C.01. — Inverse split tunnel in remote access VPN systems

prop.name: topic
prop.value: Inverse split tunnel in remote access VPN systems

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST undertake a threat and risk assessment on the use of inverse split tunnelling prior to enabling the functionality in remote access VPN systems.

control.title: 18.7.14.C.02. — Inverse split tunnel in remote access VPN systems

prop.name: topic
prop.value: Inverse split tunnel in remote access VPN systems

part.name: statement
part.p: When providing inverse split-tunnelled access to internet based services (“directly accessed services”), the following aspects SHOULD be considered as part of the threat and risk assessment:

ul.li: How do directly accessed services authenticate agency device identities prior to granting access to the service?
How do agency devices securely resolve internet addresses for directly accessed services?
How are the communications between the devices and directly accessed services secured?
How does an agency monitor and account for access made to directly accessed services?
How does an agency protect devices from compromise if they are able to directly access internet based resources, or be directly accessed from the internet?
How do directly accessed services authenticate the user of the agency device prior to granting access to the service (this is separate to authenticating the agency device itself)?
How does an agency enforce the use of multi-factor authentication with directly accessed services?

How does an agency authorise access to directly accessed services, and does this include from devices that are not authorised to connect to agency remote access services (authorisation and authentication are separate activities)?
How is access to directly accessed cloud services removed when staff no longer require access or leave the agency?

part.name: statement
part.p: When agencies have cascaded connections between networks involving multiple gateways they MUST ensure that the assurance levels specified for network devices between the overall lowest and highest networks are met by the gateway between the highest network and the next highest network within the cascaded connection.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST ensure that:

ul.li: all agency networks are protected from networks in other security domains by one or more gateways;
all gateways contain mechanisms to filter or limit data flow at the network and content level to only the information necessary for business purposes; and
all gateway components, discrete and virtual, are physically located within an appropriately secured server room.

part.name: statement
part.p: For gateways between networks in different security domains, any shared components MUST be managed by the system owners of the highest security domain or by a mutually agreed party.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST ensure that gateways:

ul.li: are the only communications paths into and out of internal networks;
by default, deny all connections into and out of the network;
allow only explicitly authorised connections;
are managed via a secure path isolated from all connected networks (i.e. physically at the gateway or on a dedicated administration network);
provide sufficient logging and audit capabilities to detect information security incidents, attempted intrusions or anomalous usage patterns; and
provide real-time alerts.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST ensure that all gateways connecting networks in different security domains:

ul.li: include a firewall of an appropriate assurance level on all gateways to filter and log network traffic attempting to enter the gateway;
are configured to save event logs to a separate, secure log server;
are protected by authentication, logging and audit of all physical access to gateway components; and
have all controls tested to verify their effectiveness after any changes to their configuration.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD use demilitarised zones to house systems and information directly accessed externally.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST perform a risk assessment on gateways and their configuration prior to their implementation.

part.name: statement
part.p: All domain and system owners connected through a gateway MUST understand and accept the residual security risk of the gateway and from any connected domains including those via a cascaded connection.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD annually review the security architecture of the gateway and risks of all connected domains including those via a cascaded connection.

part.name: statement
part.p: Once connectivity is established, domain owners SHOULD be considered information stakeholders for all connected domains.

part.name: statement
part.p: All system users SHOULD be trained in the secure use and security risks of the gateways before being granted access.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST limit access to gateway administration functions.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST ensure that system administrators are formally trained to manage gateways by qualified trainers.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST ensure that all system administrators of gateways that process NZEO information meet the nationality requirements for these endorsements.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD separate roles for the administration of gateways (e.g. separate network and security policy configuration roles).

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST authenticate system users to all classified networks accessed through gateways.

part.name: statement

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD use multi-factor authentication for access to networks and gateways.

part.name: statement

part.name: statement

part.p: Agencies SHOULD undertake a risk assessment and update the SRMP before changes are implemented.

part.name: statement

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies intending to adopt VoIP or UC technologies or services MUST conduct a comprehensive risk assessment before implementation or adoption.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies intending to adopt VoIP or UC technologies or services MUST consider the risks to the availability of systems and information in their design of VoIP and UC systems architecture, fault tolerance, fail over and supporting controls and governance processes.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST ensure risks for any VoIP or UC service adopted are understood and formally accepted by the agency’s Accreditation Authority as part of the Certification and Accreditation process (See Chapter 4 - System Certification and Accreditation).

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies intending to adopt VoIP or UC technologies or services MUST determine where the responsibility (agency or VoIP and UC service provider) for implementing, managing and maintaining controls lies in accordance with agreed trust boundaries.

part.name: statement
part.p: Any contracts for the provision of VoIP or UC services MUST include service level, availability, recoverability and restoration provisions as formally determined by business requirements.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST ensure contracts with VoIP or UC service providers include provisions to manage risks associated with the merger, acquisition, liquidation or bankruptcy of the service provider and any subsequent termination of VoIP or UC services.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies procuring or using VoIP or UC services to be used by multiple agencies MUST ensure all interested parties formally agree to the risks, controls and any residual risks of such VoIP and UC services. The lead agency normally has this responsibility (see Chapter 2 - Information Security services within Government and Chapter 4 - System Certification and Accreditation).

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD consider the use of assessment tools, such as penetration testing, when undertaking the risk assessment.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST follow the gateway requirements described in Chapter 19 - Gateway Security.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies intending to adopt VoIP or UC technologies or services MUST determine trust boundaries before implementation.

part.name: statement
part.p: Updates to the SBC and related devices MUST be verified by the administrator to ensure they are obtained from a trusted source and are unaltered.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST include defence mechanisms for the Common VoIP and UC Security Risks and Threats described in 19.5.10.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agency networks MUST ensure the SBC includes a topology hiding capability.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agency networks MUST consider the use of call diversity and call failover configurations.

part.name: statement
part.p: In a virtualised environment, agencies MUST ensure any data contained in a protected resource is deleted or not available when the virtual resource is reallocated.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD conduct a traffic analysis to ensure the agency’s network and architecture is capable of supporting all VoIP, media and UC traffic. The traffic analysis SHOULD also determine any high availability requirements.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD design a security and gateway architecture that segregates UC and normal data traffic. Firewall requirements (Section 19.3 - Firewalls) continue to apply to data traffic.

part.name: statement
part.p: In a virtualised environment, agencies SHOULD create separate virtual LANs for data traffic and UC traffic.

part.name: statement
part.p: In a non-virtualised environment, agencies SHOULD create separate LANs for data traffic and UC traffic.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agency networks SHOULD use encryption internally on VoIP and unified communications traffic.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agency networks SHOULD ensure intrusion prevention systems and firewalls are VoIP-aware.

part.name: statement
part.p: Any shared facilities MUST be clearly identifiable both physically and logically.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST provide a protected communication channel for administrators, and authorised systems personnel. Such communication MUST be logged.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST ensure administrative access to the SBC is available only through a trusted LAN and secure communication path.

part.name: statement
part.p: Access control and password requirements SHOULD apply to VoIP and UC networks in all cases where individual access is granted.

part.name: statement
part.p: In special cases where individual UserIDs and Passwords are impractical, a risk assessment SHOULD be completed and compensating controls applied.

part.name: statement
part.p: Event logs covering all VoIP and UC services SHOULD be maintained in accordance with the requirements of the NZISM. See sections 16.6 - Event Logging and Auditing and 13.1.12 - Archiving.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST include incident handling and management services in contracts with service providers.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST develop and implement incident identification and management processes in accordance with this manual (See Chapter 6 – Information Security Monitoring, Chapter 7 – Information Security Incidents, Chapter 9 – Personnel Security and Chapter 16 – Access control and passwords).

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD implement fraud detection monitoring to identify suspicious activity and provide alerting so that remedial action can be taken.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD regularly review call detail records for patterns of service theft.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD consider the use of allow and deny listing to manage fraudulent calls to known fraudulent call destinations.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD consider the use of call rate limiting as a fraud mitigation measure.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD consider the use of call redirection to manage blocked calls.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST develop and implement user awareness and training programmes to support and enable safe use of VoIP and UC services (See Section 9.1 – Information Security Awareness and Training).

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST NOT use public or hybrid (incorporating a public element) cloud services to host, process, store or transmit NZEO endorsed information.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies intending to adopt cloud technologies or services SHOULD obtain formal assurance cloud service providers will apply the controls specified in this manual to any cloud service hosting, processing or storing agency data and systems.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies intending to adopt cloud technologies or services MUST conduct a risk assessment before implementation or adoption.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies intending to adopt cloud technologies or services MUST determine trust boundaries before implementation.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies intending to adopt cloud technologies or services MUST determine where the responsibility (agency or cloud service provider) for implementing, managing and maintaining controls lies in accordance with agreed trust boundaries.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST ensure cloud risks for any cloud service adopted are understood and formally accepted by the Agency Head or Chief Executive (or their formal delegate) and the agency’s Accreditation Authority.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST consult with the GCDO to ensure the strategic and other cloud risks are comprehensively assessed.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies procuring or using cloud services to be used by multiple agencies MUST ensure all interested parties formally agree the risks, controls and any residual risks of such cloud services.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies using cloud services MUST ensure they have conducted a documented risk assessment, accepted any residual risks, and followed the endorsement procedure required by the GCDO.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies using cloud services hosted offshore MUST ensure jurisdictional, sovereignty and privacy risks are fully considered and formally accepted by the Agency Head or Chief Executive and the agency’s Accreditation Authority.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies using cloud services hosted offshore MUST ensure that the agency retains ownership of its information in any contract with the cloud service provider.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies using cloud services hosted offshore and connected to All-of-Government systems MUST ensure they have conducted a risk assessment, accepted any residual risks, and followed the endorsement procedure required by the GCDO.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST NOT use cloud services hosted offshore for information with an NZEO endorsement.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD NOT use cloud services hosted offshore unless:

ul.li: privacy, information sensitivity and information value has been fully assessed by the agency;
a comprehensive risk assessment is undertaken by the agency;
controls to manage identified risks have been specified by the agency; and
the cloud service provider is able to provide adequate assurance that these controls have been properly implemented before the agency uses the cloud service.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies intending to adopt cloud technologies or services MUST consider the risks to the availability of systems and information in their design of cloud systems architectures and supporting controls and governance processes.

part.name: statement
part.p: Any contracts for the provision of cloud services MUST include service level, availability, recoverability and restoration provisions.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST ensure contracts with cloud service providers include provisions to manage risks associated with the merger, acquisition, liquidation or bankruptcy of the service provider and any subsequent termination of cloud services.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies intending to adopt cloud technologies or services SHOULD ensure cloud service providers apply the physical, virtual and access controls specified in this manual for agency systems and data protection.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies intending to adopt cloud technologies or services SHOULD apply separation and access controls to protect data and systems where support is provided by offshore technical staff.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies intending to adopt cloud technologies or services SHOULD apply controls to detect and prevent unauthorised data transfers and multiple or large scale data transfers to offshore locations and entities.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies intending to adopt cloud technologies or services SHOULD consider the use of encryption for data in transit and at rest.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST include incident handling and management services in contracts with cloud service providers.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST develop and implement incident identification and management processes in accordance with this manual (See Chapter 6 – Information Security Monitoring, Chapter 7 – Information Security Incidents, Chapter 9 – Personnel Security and Chapter 16 – Access Control).

group.title: Backup, Recovery Archiving and Data Remanence

prop.name: topic

part.p: Agencies MUST develop and implement a backup, recovery and archiving plan and supporting procedures (See Section 6.4 – Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery).

control.title: 20.1.26.C.02. — Backup, Recovery Archiving and Data Remanence

prop.name: topic
prop.value: Backup, Recovery Archiving and Data Remanence

part.p: Agencies MUST include a data purge or secure delete process in any cloud service contracts.

prop.name: topic
prop.value: Backup, Recovery Archiving and Data Remanence

part.name: statement
part.p: Any data purge or secure delete process in any cloud service contracts MUST be independently verifiable.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST develop and implement user awareness and training programmes to support and enable safe use of cloud services (See Section 9.1 – Information Security Awareness and Training).

part.name: statement
part.p: Virtualisation technology MUST NOT be used for functional segregation between servers of different classifications.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD ensure that functional segregation between servers is achieved by:

ul.li: physically, using single dedicated machines for each function; or
using virtualisation technology to create separate virtual machines for each function within the same security domain.

part.name: statement
part.p: Virtualisation technology SHOULD NOT be used for functional segregation between servers in different security domains at the same classification.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD undertake a virtualisation specific risk assessment in order to identify risks and related risk treatments.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD architect virtualised systems and environments to enforce the principles of separation and segregation of key elements of the system using trust zones.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD design virtualised systems and environments to enable functional segregation within a security domain.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD harden the host operating systems following an agency or other approved hardening guide.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD separate production from test or development virtual environments.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD NOT permit the sharing of files or other operating system components between host and guest operating systems.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD ensure a VM migration policy and related SOPs are implemented.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD implement controls to prohibit unauthorised VM migrations within a virtual environment or between physical environments.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD implement controls to safely decommission VMs when no longer required.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD implement security and operational management and monitoring tools which include the following minimum capabilities:

ul.li: Identify VMs when initiated;
Validate integrity of files prior to installation;
Scan new VMs for vulnerabilities and misconfigurations;
Load only minimum operating system components and services;
Set resource usage limits;
Establish connections to peripherals only as required;
Ensure host and guest time synchronisation;
Detect snapshot rollbacks and scans after restores;
Track asset migration; and
Monitor the security posture of migrated assets.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST maintain strong physical security and physical access controls.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST maintain strong authentication and access controls.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD maintain strong data validation checks.

part.name: statement
part.p: The principles of separation and segregation MUST be applied to the design and architecture of VLANs.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST NOT use VLANs between any classified network and any unclassified network.

part.name: statement
part.p: VLAN trunking MUST NOT be used on switches managing VLANs of differing security domains.

part.name: statement
part.p: Administrative access MUST be permitted only from the most trusted network.

part.name: statement
part.p: Unused ports on the switches SHOULD be disabled.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST establish a policy and train staff in the processes for data transfers between systems and the authorisations required before transfers can take place.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST ensure that system users transferring data to and from a system are held accountable for the data they transfer.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD ensure that data transfers are performed in accordance with processes and procedures approved by the Accreditation Authority.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies importing data to a system MUST ensure that the data is scanned for malicious and active content.

group.title: Preventing export of NZEO data to foreign systems

control.title: 21.1.13.C.01. — Preventing export of NZEO data to foreign systems

prop.name: topic
prop.value: Preventing export of NZEO data to foreign systems

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST:

ul.li: ensure that keyword searches are performed on all textual data;
ensure that any identified data is quarantined until reviewed and approved for release by a trusted source other than the originator; and
develop procedures to prevent NZEO information in both textual and non-textual formats from being exported.

part.name: statement
part.p: Users transferring data to and from a system MUST be held accountable for the data they transfer.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD restrict the export of data to a system of a lesser classification by filtering data using at least protective marking checks.

group.title: Preventing export of NZEO data to foreign systems

control.title: 21.2.10.C.01. — Preventing export of NZEO data to foreign systems

prop.name: topic
prop.value: Preventing export of NZEO data to foreign systems

part.name: statement
part.p: To prevent the export of NZEO data to foreign systems, agencies MUST implement NZEO data filtering performed by a product specifically designed or configured for that purpose.

control.title: 21.2.10.C.02. — Preventing export of NZEO data to foreign systems

prop.name: topic
prop.value: Preventing export of NZEO data to foreign systems

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST undertake checks of protective markings and keywords before permitting data export.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD strictly define and limit the types of files that can be transferred based on business requirements and the results of a security risk assessment.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD block all executables and active content from being communicated though gateways.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST block, quarantine or drop any data identified by a data filter as suspicious until reviewed and approved for transfer by a trusted source other than the originator.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD perform validation on all data passing through a content filter, blocking content which fails the validation.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD perform content conversion, file conversion or both for all ingress or egress data transiting a security domain boundary.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD perform content and file sanitisation on suitable file types if content conversion or file conversion is not appropriate for data transiting a security domain boundary.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD perform antivirus scans on all content using up-to-date engines and signatures, using multiple different scanning engines.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD extract the contents from archive and container files and subject the extracted files to content filter tests.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD perform controlled inspection of archive and container files to ensure that content filter performance and availability is not adversely affected.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD block files that cannot be inspected and generate an alert or notification.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD create and enforce an allow list of permitted content types based on business requirements and the results of a security risk assessment.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD verify the integrity of content where applicable, and block the content if verification fails.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD decrypt and inspect all encrypted content, traffic and data to allow content filtering.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST use protective marking checks to restrict the export of data from each security domain, including through a gateway.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD create an exception handling process to deal with blocked or quarantined file types that may have a valid requirement to be transferred.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD ensure that all classified information stored within a database is associated with an appropriate protective marking if the information:

ul.li: could be exported to a different system; or
contains differing classifications or different handling requirements.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD ensure that protective markings are applied with a level of granularity sufficient to clearly define the handling requirements for any classified information retrieved or exported from a database.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD protect database files from access that bypass normal access controls.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD ensure that databases provide functionality to allow for auditing of system users’ actions.

part.name: statement
part.p: If results from database queries cannot be appropriately filtered, agencies MUST ensure that all query results are appropriately sanitised to meet the minimum security clearances of system users.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD ensure that system users who do not have sufficient security clearances to view database contents cannot see or interrogate associated metadata in a list of results from a search engine query.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST develop a policy governing the use of mobile devices.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD implement a Mobile Device Management (MDM) solution.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST advise personnel of the maximum permitted classifications for data and voice communications when using mobile devices.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD NOT use Paging Services, SMS or MMS for sensitive or classified communications.

group.title: Non-agency owned and controlled mobile devices

control.title: 22.1.12.C.01. — Non-agency owned and controlled mobile devices

prop.name: topic
prop.value: Non-agency owned and controlled mobile devices

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST apply the full set of BYOD controls for devices NOT directly owned and controlled by the agency. These controls are detailed in Section 21.4 – BYOD.

prop.name: topic
prop.value: Agency owned mobile device storage encryption

control.title: 22.1.13.C.03. — Agency owned mobile device storage encryption

prop.name: topic
prop.value: Agency owned mobile device storage encryption

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies unable to lower the storage and physical transfer requirements of a mobile device to an unclassified level through the use of encryption SHOULD physically store or transfer the device as a classified asset in accordance with the relevant handling instructions.

prop.name: topic
prop.value: Agency owned mobile device storage encryption

prop.name: topic
prop.value: Agency owned mobile device storage encryption

part.name: statement
part.p: Pool or shared devices SHOULD be reissued with unique passwords, passphrases, PINs or other access codes for each separate issue or deployment.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST use encryption on mobile devices communicating over public infrastructure, the Internet or non-agency controlled networks.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD use encryption for Official Information or any classified information on mobile devices communicating over public infrastructure, the Internet or non-agency controlled networks.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD apply privacy filters to the screens of mobile devices.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD NOT enable Bluetooth functionality on mobile devices.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agency personnel MUST NOT disable security functions or security configurations on a mobile device once provisioned.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD control the configuration of mobile devices in the same manner as devices in the agency’s office environment.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD prevent personnel from installing unauthorised applications on a mobile device once provisioned.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD ensure that mobile devices have security updates applied on a regular basis and are tested to ensure that the mobile devices are still secure.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD conduct policy checks as mobile devices connect to agency systems.

group.title: Connecting mobile devices to the Internet

control.title: 22.1.19.C.01. — Connecting mobile devices to the Internet

prop.name: topic
prop.value: Connecting mobile devices to the Internet

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST disable split tunnelling when using a VPN connection from a mobile device to connect to an agency network.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST develop an emergency destruction plan for mobile devices.

part.name: statement
part.p: If a cryptographic zeroise or sanitise function is provided for cryptographic keys on a mobile device it MUST be used as part of the emergency destruction procedures.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD ensure personnel are trained in emergency destruction procedures and are familiar with the emergency destruction plan.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD use soft labelling for mobile devices when appropriate to reduce their attractiveness value.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD develop a policy to manage the non-business or personal use of an agency owned device.

part.name: statement
part.p: Mobile devices SHOULD NOT be used other than by personnel specifically authorised by the agency.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST NOT allow personnel to access or communicate classified information on mobile devices outside of secure areas unless there is a reduced chance of being overheard and having the screen of the device observed.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies allowing personnel to access or communicate classified information outside of the office SHOULD NOT allow personnel to do so in public locations (e.g. public transport, transit lounges, hotel lobbies and coffee shops).

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST ensure mobile devices are carried in a secured state when not being actively used, by:

ul.li: power off; or
power on but pass code enabled.

part.name: statement
part.p: When in use mobile devices MUST be kept under continual direct supervision.

part.name: statement
part.p: When travelling with mobile devices and media, personnel MUST retain control over them at all times including by not placing them in checked-in luggage or leaving them unattended.

part.name: statement
part.p: Travelling personnel requested to decrypt mobile devices for inspection or from whom mobile devices are taken out of sight by border control MUST report the potential compromise of classified information or the device to an ITSM as soon as possible.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST ensure that when mobile devices are not being actively used they are secured in accordance with the minimum physical security requirements as stated in the PSR.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST ensure that the area within which mobile devices are used meets the minimum physical security requirements as stated in the PSR.

group.title: 22.4 Non-Agency Owned Devices and Bring Your Own Device (BYOD)

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST undertake a risk assessment and implement appropriate controls BEFORE implementing a BYOD Policy and permitting the use of BYOD.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST take an integrated approach to BYOD security, covering policy, training, support, systems architecture, security, systems management, change management, incident detection & management and business continuity.

part.name: statement
part.p: BYOD MUST only be permitted for agency information systems up to and including RESTRICTED.

part.name: statement
part.p: Devices that have been “jail-broken”, “rooted” or have settings violations MUST NOT be used for any agency business or be allowed to connect to any agency systems UNLESS this been specifically authorised.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies may identify additional policy provisions and controls that are required, based on their assessment of risk. Agencies MUST implement the additional controls and protocols before implementing BYOD.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST implement a BYOD acceptable use policy, agreed and signed by each person using a BYOD device.

part.name: statement
part.p: The agency’s policy MUST clearly establish eligibility of personnel for participation in the agency BYOD scheme.

part.name: statement
part.p: Personnel MUST have written authorisation (usually managerial approval) before a connection is enabled (on-boarding).

part.name: statement
part.p: Written authorisation MUST include the nature and extent of agency access approved, considering:

ul.li: time, day of the week;
location; and
local or roaming access.

part.name: statement
part.p: Procedures MUST be established for removal of agency installed software and any agency data when the user no longer has a need to use BYOD, is redeployed or ceases employment (off-boarding).

part.name: statement
part.p: Standard Operating Procedures for the agency’s BYOD network MUST be established.

part.name: statement
part.p: Provision MUST be made for contractors and other authorised non-employees. It is at the agency’s discretion whether this activity is permitted. The risk assessment MUST reflect this factor.

part.name: statement
part.p: Ownership of data on BYOD devices MUST be clearly articulated and agreed.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agency policies MUST clearly articulate the separation between corporate support and where individuals are responsible for the maintenance and support of their own devices.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agency policies MUST clearly articulate the acceptable use of any GPS or other tracking capability.

part.name: statement
part.p: Individual responsibility for the cost of any BYOD device and its accessories MUST be agreed.

part.name: statement
part.p: Individual responsibility for replacement in the event of loss or theft MUST be agreed.

part.name: statement
part.p: Individuals MUST be responsible for the installation and maintenance of any mandated BYOD-based firewalls and anti-malware software and for implementing operating system updates and patches on their device.

part.name: statement
part.p: The procedures for purchasing and installing business related applications on the mobile devices MUST be specified and agreed.

part.name: statement
part.p: The responsibility for payment of voice and data plans and roaming charges MUST be specified and agreed.

part.name: statement
part.p: A security architectural review MUST be undertaken by the agency before allowing BYOD devices to connect to agency systems.

part.name: statement
part.p: The BYOD network segment MUST be segregated from other elements of the agency’s network.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST architecturally separate guest and public facing networks from BYOD networks.

part.name: statement
part.p: Network configuration policies and authentication mechanisms MUST allow access to agency resources ONLY through the BYOD network segment.

part.name: statement
part.p: Access to internal resources and servers MUST be carefully managed and confined to only those services for which there is a defined and properly authorised business requirement.

part.name: statement
part.p: Wireless access points used for access to agency networks MUST be implemented and secured in accordance with the directions in this manual (See Section 18.2 – Wireless Local Area Networks).

part.name: statement
part.p: Bluetooth on BYOD devices MUST be disabled while within designated secure areas on agency premises.

part.name: statement
part.p: Access Controls MUST be implemented in accordance with Chapter 16 – Access Control.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST maintain a list of permitted operating systems, including operating system version numbers, for BYOD devices.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST check each BYOD device for malware and sanitise the device appropriately before installing agency software or operating environments.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST check each BYOD device for malware and sanitise the device appropriately before permitting access to agency data.

part.name: statement
part.p: BYOD MUST have a Mobile Device Management (MDM) solution implemented with a minimum of the following enabled:

ul.li: The MDM is enabled to “wipe” devices of any agency data if lost or stolen;
If the MDM cannot discriminate between agency and personal data, all data, including personal data, is deleted if the device is lost or stolen;
The MDM is capable of remotely applying agency security configurations for BYOD devices;
Mobile device security configurations are validated (health check) by the MDM before a device is permitted to connect to the agency’s systems;
“Jail-broken”, “rooted” or settings violations MUST be detected and isolated;
“Jail-broken” devices are NOT permitted to access agency resources;
Access to agency resources is limited until both the device and user is fully compliant with policy and SOPs;
Auditing and logging is enabled; and
Changes of Subscriber Identity Module (SIM) card are monitored to allow remote blocking and wiping in the event of theft or compromise.

part.name: statement
part.p: Intrusion detection systems MUST be implemented.

part.name: statement
part.p: Continuous monitoring MUST be established to detect actual or potential security compromises or incidents from BYOD devices. Refer also to Chapter 6 - Information Security Monitoring.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST maintain a list of approved cloud applications that may be used on BYOD devices.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST block the use of unapproved cloud applications for processing any agency or organisational data.

part.name: statement
part.p: BYOD devices MUST NOT be permitted direct connection to internal hosts, including all other devices on the local network.

part.name: statement
part.p: BYOD devices connecting to guest and public facing networks MUST NOT be permitted access to the corporate network other than through a VPN over the Internet.

part.name: statement
part.p: Bluetooth on BYOD devices SHOULD be disabled while within agency premises and while accessing agency systems and data.

part.name: statement
part.p: BYOD devices and systems SHOULD use Multi-factor (at least two-factor) authentication to connect to agency systems and prior to being permitted access to agency data.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST implement a wireless IDS /IPS on BYOD wireless networks.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST implement rogue AP and wireless “hot spot” detection and implement response procedures where detection occurs.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD conduct a baseline survey to identify:

ul.li: All authorised devices and AP’s; and
Any unauthorised devices and AP’s.

part.name: statement
part.p: Any agency data exchanged with the mobile device MUST be encrypted in transit (See Chapter 17 – Cryptography).

part.name: statement
part.p: Any agency data stored on the device MUST be encrypted (including keys, certificates and other essential session establishment data).

part.name: statement
part.p: The use of virtual containers, sandboxes, wraps or similar mechanisms on the mobile device MUST be established for each authorised session for any organisational data. These mechanisms MUST be non-persistent and be removed at the end of each session.

part.name: statement
part.p: Any sensitive agency data MUST be removed and securely deleted, or encrypted at the end of a session.

part.name: statement
part.p: Connections to the agency network MUST be time limited to avoid leaving a session “logged on”.

part.name: statement
part.p: Communications between the mobile device and the agency network MUST be established through a Virtual Private Network (VPN).

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST disable split-tunnelling when using a BYOD device to connect to an agency network (See Section 21.1 – Agency Owned Mobile Devices).

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST disable the ability for a BYOD device to establish simultaneous connections (e.g. wireless and cellular) when connected to an agency’s network.

part.name: statement
part.p: The use of passwords or PINs to unlock the BYOD device MUST be enforced in addition to all other agency authentication mechanisms.

part.name: statement
part.p: BYOD device passwords MUST be distinct from any agency access and authentication passwords.

part.name: statement
part.p: BYOD passwords MUST be distinct from other fixed or mobile agency network passwords (See Section 16.1 – Identification and Authentication for details on password requirements).

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD compile a list of approved BYOD devices and operating systems for the guidance of staff.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD consider the implementation of Data Loss Prevention (DLP) technologies.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD consider the use of bandwidth limits as a means of controlling data downloads and uploads.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD take legal advice on the provisions in their BYOD policy.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST clearly identify and understand where classification, security domain, and trust zone boundaries exist prior to implementation or adoption of public cloud services.

part.name: statement
part.p: Where multiple identity systems under different security policies are used to control access to an agency’s instance of a public cloud service, the instance MUST be considered to be in a separate security domain from services where access control is managed solely by the agency’s identity system.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST clearly identify and understand their cloud service provider’s security responsibilities for each service consumed, and the aspects of security that the agency is responsible for, prior to implementation or adoption of the service.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD clearly document the aspects of security they and their provider are responsible for.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD review existing security processes to ensure compatibility with their cloud service provider’s responsibilities.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD deploy and manage their cloud infrastructure using automation, version control, and infrastructure as code techniques where these are available.

group.title: Understanding levels of assurance for public cloud

control.title: 23.2.16.C.01. — Understanding levels of assurance for public cloud

prop.name: topic
prop.value: Understanding levels of assurance for public cloud

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST update their risk assessment process to account for public cloud specific risks, prior to implementation or adoption of public cloud services.

control.title: 23.2.16.C.02. — Understanding levels of assurance for public cloud

prop.name: topic
prop.value: Understanding levels of assurance for public cloud

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST undertake a cloud specific risk assessment in line with the process outlined by the GCDO for each public cloud service, prior to implementation or adoption of public cloud services.

control.title: 23.2.16.C.04. — Understanding levels of assurance for public cloud

prop.name: topic
prop.value: Understanding levels of assurance for public cloud

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST NOT accredit public cloud services to host, process, store, or transmit NZEO endorsed information.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST consider risks to the availability of systems and information in their design of cloud systems architectures, supporting controls, and governance processes prior to implementation or adoption of public cloud services.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD obtain regular assurance checks on cloud service providers, ensuring they have been undertaken by a suitably qualified assessor.

group.title: Cloud service providers – patching and software maintenance

control.title: 23.2.19.C.01. — Cloud service providers – patching and software maintenance

prop.name: topic
prop.value: Cloud service providers – patching and software maintenance

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST obtain assurance that cloud service providers undertake appropriate software and operating system patching and maintenance.

group.title: Assurance around workload isolation on shared infrastructure

control.title: 23.2.20.C.01. — Assurance around workload isolation on shared infrastructure

prop.name: topic
prop.value: Assurance around workload isolation on shared infrastructure

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST obtain assurance that technical protections exist to adequately isolate tenants.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD make use of the GCSB endorsed baseline security templates where applicable.

part.name: statement
part.p: Accounts used to perform privileged actions SHOULD NOT be synchronised between environments.

part.name: statement
part.p: Where administration interfaces or portals are accessible from the internet, privileged accounts MUST be configured to use multiple factors of authentication.

part.name: statement
part.p: Where cloud service interfaces or portals are accessible from the internet, user accounts SHOULD be configured to use multiple factors of authentication.

part.name: statement
part.p: Staff offboarding processes MUST be updated to include removing all access to public cloud based services, prior to implementation or adoption of public cloud services.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST ensure that relying parties continually verify the authenticity of their identity provider’s responses, through for example, cryptographic signing of authentication requests and responses.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD ensure that relying parties use all available information from the identity provider to inform access control decisions.

part.name: statement
part.p: For each cloud service, agencies MUST ensure that the mechanisms used to protect data meet agency requirements.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST update key management plans to account for differences in public cloud before storing organisational data in a public cloud environment.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST ensure their key management plan includes provision for migrating data from the cloud environment where it was created.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST apply the principle of least privilege and configure service endpoints to restrict access to authorised parties.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST identify where data used in conjunction with a public cloud service is stored or processed, including any replicas or backups that may be created.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agency risk assessments of public cloud services MUST include any risks arising from data location. Any actions required to mitigate these risks must be identified and documented prior to implementation or adoption of public cloud services.

group.title: Revise disaster recovery plans to include data in public cloud

control.title: 23.4.12.C.01. — Revise disaster recovery plans to include data in public cloud

prop.name: topic
prop.value: Revise disaster recovery plans to include data in public cloud

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST update their disaster recovery plans prior to storing or replicating data in public cloud services, to ensure these plans address any cloud-specific aspects of backup and recovery.

control.title: 23.4.12.C.02. — Revise disaster recovery plans to include data in public cloud

prop.name: topic
prop.value: Revise disaster recovery plans to include data in public cloud

part.name: statement
part.p: When planning tests of disaster recovery processes in accordance with 6.4.6 Backup strategy, agencies MUST include tests of any cloud-specific data recovery processes.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST have a defined exit strategy for each public cloud service they consume, including a process by which their data can be retrieved and erased from the cloud service as part of contract termination.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST ensure all data they need to retain is retrieved from the cloud service provider prior to decommissioning.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST have assurance that no agency-owned data is retained on the cloud service being decommissioned.

group.title: 23.5 Logging and Alerting in Public Cloud

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST understand the range of logging capabilities provided by their cloud service providers and determine whether they are sufficient for agency needs.

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST ensure that logs associated with public cloud services are collected, protected, and that their integrity can be confirmed in accordance with the agency’s documented logging requirements.

group.title: Detecting information security incidents in public cloud

control.title: 23.5.12.C.01. — Detecting information security incidents in public cloud

prop.name: topic
prop.value: Detecting information security incidents in public cloud

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies MUST ensure that cloud service provider logs are incorporated into overall enterprise logging and alerting systems or procedures in a timely manner to detect information security incidents.

control.title: 23.5.12.C.02. — Detecting information security incidents in public cloud

prop.name: topic
prop.value: Detecting information security incidents in public cloud

part.name: statement
part.p: Agencies SHOULD ensure that tools and procedures used to detect potential information security incidents account for the public cloud services being consumed by the agency.
